patch.statement: 実内積空間（$0$でない）上のアフィン空間で、中心$O_1,O_2$、半径$r_1,r_2$の2つの球面（平面なら2円）について、第1の球面が第2の球面に内接する（共有点$T$があり、$O_1$が線分$O_2T$上にある）ことと、$O_1O_2=r_2-r_1$かつ$r_1,r_2\geq0$は同値である。なお同一の球面（$O_1=O_2$かつ$r_1=r_2$）や半径$0$の球面も、この定義では内接に含める。
patch.statement_en: In a nonzero real inner product affine space, the sphere with center O1 and radius r1 is internally tangent to the sphere with center O2 and radius r2, meaning that some common point T has O1 on segment O2T, if and only if |O1O2| = r2 - r1 and r1, r2 ≥ 0. Coincident spheres and spheres of radius 0 count as internally tangent under this definition.

hard_negative.statement: $\angle ACB=\angle A'C'B'$、$AB=A'B'$、$BC=B'C'$ならば、$A,B,C$と$A',B',C'$は合同である。

patch.statement: $A,B,C$と$A',B',C'$がこの対応で相似ならば、対応する辺の比を積の形で書いた等式$AB\cdot B'C'=A'B'\cdot BC$、$BC\cdot C'A'=B'C'\cdot CA$、$CA\cdot A'B'=C'A'\cdot AB$が成り立つ。 ここで相似とは、対応する2頂点間の距離の比がすべて同じ正の数であることをいう。
patch.statement_en: If A, B, C and A', B', C' are similar in this order, then AB·B'C' = A'B'·BC, BC·C'A' = B'C'·CA and CA·A'B' = C'A'·AB. Here similar means that all pairwise distances of corresponding vertices have the same positive ratio.

patch.statement: 三角形$ABC$と三角形$A'B'C'$（それぞれ3点は同一直線上にない）と正の数$r$について、$AB=r\,A'B'$、$BC=r\,B'C'$、$CA=r\,C'A'$ならば、2辺とその間の角の正弦で表した面積の式について$\frac12AB\cdot BC\sin\angle ABC=r^2\cdot\frac12A'B'\cdot B'C'\sin\angle A'B'C'$が成り立つ。

findings.issue: Same pattern as geometry_circle.thales_right_angle_iff_on_diameter_circle (angle = pi/2 iff A on the circle with diameter BC; here with M as centre) and school_vectors_complex.circle_diameter_inner_zero. Target is correct including the degenerate A=B case because the text defines the right angle via the inner product.

systemic: Planarity is dropped in OpenMath: 16 circle cards carry [Fact (finrank R V = 2)] in the target but their OpenMath has no euclidean_plane_ambient (used by geometry_centers); for 7 of them (right_angle..chord_is_diameter, chord_eq_two_radius_sin..., equal_inscribed_angles..., contact_chord..., common_chord..., two_circles_at_most_two..., two_circles_common_point_exists...) the same OpenMath encodes a false 3D/1D statement. Patch: add euclidean_plane_ambient to the hypothesis conjunction.

Every side condition (same side vs opposite side, O vs X for central angles, T vs C for tangent-chord, A,C vs B,D for cyclic quadrilaterals) was checked against the target, the hard_negative coordinates and the answer; all are correct and strict (points not on the line). Unoriented angles are used throughout, consistent with the side predicates; no oriented-angle cards exist.

perpendicular_lines / parallel_lines are used in OpenMath where Lean uses inner-product or AffineSubspace.Parallel and where the two defining points can coincide (A=H, B=C, midpoint cards); inner_product (as in circle 8, 15, 16) is the faithful encoding. Also tangent_to_circle_at (t p c r) and line_tangent_to_circle_at (a b t c r) express the same concept (the first is the second with a=t); and on_circle is used for spheres in all dimensions. Unify the tangent symbol and consider on_sphere.

Definition-based cards: Congruent and Similar are Mathlib's distance-based definitions and 'tangent' is the orthRadius definition, so SSS-congruence, 'tangent <-> perpendicular radius' and the SSS-similarity first conjunct are definitional; statements that use 相似 must define it (4 cards do not).

Hard negatives for SSA-type failures (SAS, HL, SAS-similarity, bisector-feet) state existence of a counterexample without numbers; concrete values give the checkable form. All coordinate hard negatives in the circle domain were checked by hand with the stated coordinates.

Cross-domain duplicates: Thales (circle thales..., triangle right_angle_iff_median_half_hypotenuse, school_vectors_complex.circle_diameter_inner_zero), altitude on hypotenuse (circle altitude_to_diameter..., triangle right_triangle_altitude_geometric_mean), incircle tangent length (circle triangle_incircle_tangent_length, geometry_centers.incircle_tangent_length), chord = 2r sin (circle chord_eq_two_radius..., geometry_centers.law_of_sines_circumradius), area ratio (triangle ..._area_ratio_sine_form, geometry_plane.area_similar_triangles_ratio_square).

Nine circle cards (inscribed angle, converse, central angle, cyclic quadrilateral, exterior angle, tangent-chord and converse) are probably true without finrank = 2 (SSameSide/SOppSide force coplanarity), but the plane form is the textbook one and stays valid; no defect, only a possible generalization.
missing_neighbors: Oriented inscribed angle theorem without side conditions: 2 • oangle p1 p2 p4 = 2 • oangle p1 p3 p4 for p2,p3,p4 on a sphere (EuclideanGeometry.Cospherical.two_zsmul_oangle_eq, Sphere.two_zsmul_oangle_eq) and its converse (cospherical_of_two_zsmul_oangle_eq_of_not_collinear).
Oriented central angle: oangle at centre = 2 • oangle on circle (EuclideanGeometry.Sphere.oangle_center_eq_two_zsmul_oangle).

Unified signed power of a point: for A,B on sphere s and H in line[A,B], inner (A -ᵥ H) (B -ᵥ H) = dist H s.center ^ 2 - s.radius ^ 2 (no inside/outside split; Mathlib Sphere.power, mul_dist_eq_abs_power).

Radical axis: for non-concentric spheres, equal power is a hyperplane perpendicular to the line of centres and contains the common points (generalizes common_chord and two_circles_at_most_two_common_points).

Power of a point stated for four cospherical points and two lines through P, any dimension (geometry_homotopy.power_of_a_point_lines exists in another domain; none here), plus the converse for crossing lines.

Law of cosines in product form valid for all points: dist A C ^ 2 = dist A B ^ 2 + dist C B ^ 2 - 2 * dist A B * dist C B * cos (angle A B C) (EuclideanGeometry.law_cos); only the divided form (needs A != B, C != B) is in this domain.
Non-strict triangle inequality with equality case: dist A C <= dist A B + dist B C, equality iff Wbtw B on AC (dist_add_dist_eq_iff); only the strict non-collinear form is here.
SSS/SAS/ASA congruence as existence of an isometry (e.g. f : P ->ᵃⁱ[R] P with f A = A', f B = B', f C = C'), since Congruent is purely distance-based.

Tangent from an external point: existence and exactly two tangent lines/points, and the tangent-length formula QT^2 = QO^2 - r^2 together with the sphere-in-plane statement that two tangents exist iff QO > r.
Existence of a triangle with given sides in a general plane ([Fact (finrank R V = 2)]), instead of EuclideanSpace R (Fin 2).
Angle bisector as the locus of points equidistant from the two side lines (Mathlib Euclidean/Angle/Bisector: dist_orthogonalProjection_eq_iff_angle_eq), the standard route to incenter facts.

Equal tangent segments from an external point to a circle together with the exterior-bisector of tangent angle (excircle/incircle contact lengths) in sphere-tangent form, to complement triangle_incircle_tangent_length.
